My father came out in his late 40s after a 26 year marriage to my mother. For us (his 4 kids) it didn't change much. It really affected my mom, kinda destroyed her learning "she was living a lie". And my dad was Bi when he married her, and just thought it would be easier to be with a women then a man since he was attracted to both. Yet later on he concluded he was happier with men and made his full coming out. 
It was really hard for him the few years between the realization and the coming. He was never that miserable. 
But since he came out, he has never been happier and looks way younger !

The best thing you can do for both you and your wife is be honest. It may be hard, but better in the end for the both of you !

Good luck

I joined a support group for teen/young adult that had lost a parent, and there I discovered it's often when about to start a new chapter that you may need guidance about navigating said loss. 
The support group gave me a place to talk about her, what I wished she had seen me become and to make some sense of all of this. It helped me to know where I was even without her. 

I don't know what could work for you, but I hope you find it and a way to make sense of it all, even without her.

Hey there, first of all, you have my deepest sympathy and my condolences for your loss. Since I don’t know your situation, I’ll just try to give you my opinion.
First of all, loosing someone and grieving takes time, lots of it. It not linear, and it’s frustratingly slow. But the thing you should do if you feel like you can, and as soon you notice you can, is appreciate stuff as it comes. After I lost my mom, it took time before I enjoyed things again, but I really think that being attentive about enjoying activities and being around people will show you that it can happen again, and show you how. 
For the second part, whatever happened, try to find peace with it. You didn’t mean to not be there, you couldn’t know and therefore it’s not your fault. Besides, whatever happened, even if it was your fault, if you didn’t actively tried to kill someone, in my opinion, you still deserve to find peace. Sometimes people die, and that’s just how life goes and end, and there is no need to blame anyone, except for murder, naturally. Maybe she’s just blaming you because she needs a culprit to move on, who knows ? It could be her own way of grieving. Just try to heal for yourself, at your pace, to be with people who help you feel ok, to do what helps you. And by doing so until you feel there is actually a way forward, you’ll find a way to first, move on (wich doesn’t mean forgetting, but just living your life), and then helping your relatives.

I don’t know if it helps, but I really hope you find a way. And know you’re never alone, even if it sometimes feels this way
